label: A2B_mC48_15_ae3f_2f-001
title: Coesite (SiO$_{2}$) Structure
comments:
This was named for its original discoverer, Loring Coes, Jr. (Coes, 1953; Hazen, 1999). 
 At 2.92 gm/cm$^{3}$ this is the densest form of silica we have found.  
 More information about SiO$_{2}$ structures can be found in our article on \href{current_web_home_dir/Tutorials/SiO2_AlPO4}{SiO$_{2}$ and AlPO$_{4}$}. 
 Our original work (Mehl, 2017) misplaced the O II Wycoff position.  This is corrected here. 
 More information about other SiO$_{2}$ and related structures can be found in our article on \href{current_web_home_dir/Tutorials/SiO2_AlPO4}{SiO$_{2}$ and AlPO$_{4}$}.
